rubric.task_read: A very long-horizon, high-complexity task: implement a complete Zstandard decoder in C purely from RFC 8878, producing byte-identical output to `zstd -d` across the full feature matrix (frame headers, three block types, all literal encodings, FSE in four modes, Huffman with FSE weights + treeless reuse, sequence machinery with repeat-offset history, multi-frame and dictionary frames). Difficulty comes from a dense binary spec that must be understood precisely, many interdependent subsystems that must be built in the right order, and correctness that is bit-exact and unforgiving — a single misread field breaks everything downstream. This warrants heavy, sustained meta-work: careful spec orientation, layered decomposition with per-component checks, a differential-testing verification strategy against the reference tool, tight progress tracking across dozens of features, and disciplined course-correction when a mis-decoded field surfaces far from its cause.

dimensions.name: Spec comprehension & format reconnaissance
dimensions.description: Reading and correctly internalizing the relevant sections of RFC 8878 before and while implementing each subsystem, and probing real .zst inputs to ground understanding.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The only source of truth is a dense binary-format spec; every field width, bit order, and table-construction rule must be read precisely. Acting from a half-remembered mental model of zstd (rather than the actual RFC text) produces subtly wrong decoders that fail bit-exact comparison in ways that are extremely hard to diagnose later.

anchors.0: Starts coding from prior/assumed knowledge of zstd; never meaningfully consults the RFC or inspects sample inputs.
anchors.3: Skims the RFC for the current feature only, reactively, and often mis-reads bit-ordering / field-width details; no examination of actual byte layouts.
anchors.5: Reads the relevant RFC section before implementing each subsystem and gets most field definitions right; occasionally dumps bytes of a sample frame to confirm structure.
anchors.8: Systematically works the RFC section by section, extracts the exact rules for tricky areas (FSE table build, Huffman weight decoding, repeat-offset LL=0 case, window/FCS field widths) and cross-checks them against hex dumps of real frames before trusting the implementation.
anchors.10: Builds a precise, verified model of the whole format up front and deepens it per subsystem: reconciles ambiguous spec passages against observed bytes, anticipates the interactions (treeless literal reuse, dictionary-preloaded entropy/offset state) from the reading, and documents the exact bit-level contract so later debugging traces cleanly back to spec clauses.

dimensions.name: Subsystem decomposition & build ordering
dimensions.description: Breaking the decoder into an ordered hierarchy of independently-checkable components (frame parse → block dispatch → literals → FSE → Huffman → sequences → offset history → dictionaries) with an explicit done-condition for each.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The subsystems have hard dependencies (sequences need FSE; Huffman literals need FSE weights; dictionaries preload entropy state). Building in the wrong order, or as one monolithic push, means nothing is verifiable until everything is done — fatal on a task this size.

anchors.0: Treats it as one undifferentiated coding effort; no visible sub-goals or ordering.
anchors.3: Vague ordering in the agent's head; components entangled so none can be tested alone; milestones are just 'write more code'.
anchors.5: Clear list of the major subsystems tackled in a sensible dependency order, each landed before moving on, with an implicit 'this feature works now' checkpoint.
anchors.8: Explicit milestone structure that respects dependencies and picks a walking-skeleton path (e.g. raw blocks / raw literals end-to-end first, then FSE, then Huffman, then sequences, then dictionaries), each milestone with a concrete done-signal (a class of inputs now decodes correctly).
anchors.10: A layered plan that sequences by both dependency and diagnostic isolation — earliest features chosen to make later ones debuggable, each subsystem given its own smallest-possible test input, and the plan re-ordered deliberately when an unexpected dependency (e.g. offset history spanning blocks) is discovered.

dimensions.name: Differential-testing & correctness verification
dimensions.description: Deliberately designing how correctness is checked — differential comparison against `zstd -d`, per-subsystem and per-input-shape test coverage, byte-exact diffs — beyond the provided `test.sh` sanity check.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Correctness is bit-exact and the visible `test.sh` covers only a handful of inputs; the grading set exercises every feature. An agent that leans only on test.sh will believe it is done while whole feature classes (8-byte FCS, treeless literals, dictionary frames, overlapping match copies) are silently broken.

anchors.0: No verification beyond 'it compiles'; or runs the binary and eyeballs output.
anchors.3: Relies solely on the provided test.sh; treats passing it as done.
anchors.5: Generates a few of its own .zst inputs and diffs decoder output against `zstd -d`, covering the common cases beyond test.sh.
anchors.8: Constructs a deliberate differential-testing harness that feeds many inputs — spanning the feature matrix (each FCS width, each block type, each literal/FSE mode, multi-frame, checksum, dictionary) — through both its decoder and `zstd -d` and compares byte-for-byte, using targeted inputs to isolate which subsystem fails.
anchors.10: Systematically enumerates the full feature matrix from the RFC and engineers inputs (or corpora) that exercise each edge — overlapping copies, LL=0 repeat-offset, treeless reuse across blocks, dictionary-preloaded state, skippable frames — with automated byte-exact comparison, adds regression cases as bugs are found, and treats an unexplained mismatch as a first-class signal rather than noise.

dimensions.name: Feature-coverage tracking & stuck detection
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which features work vs remain across the large matrix, and recognizing when debugging a single mismatch has become circular.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With dozens of interacting features and bit-exact grading, it is easy to lose the plot — to think the decoder is largely done when several feature classes are untested, or to burn the horizon re-debugging one FSE bug in circles. Accurate self-assessment decides whether the horizon is spent well.

anchors.0: No sense of overall coverage; declares done with large feature classes never exercised; or loops on one bug indefinitely with no awareness.
anchors.3: Tracks progress only implicitly; conflates 'test.sh passes' with 'complete'; little awareness of being stuck.
anchors.5: Keeps a rough checklist of features done vs remaining and notices when repeatedly failing on the same input.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit, accurate coverage map of the feature matrix (what is verified, what is untested, what is failing), and when a bug resists, steps back to re-diagnose rather than retrying the same fix.
anchors.10: Continuously reconciles claimed-done against verified-done across the whole matrix, flags untested corners honestly, detects circular debugging early and switches diagnostic tactic (narrower input, hex-level trace, re-read spec clause), keeping an accurate done-vs-remaining picture across the entire long build.

dimensions.name: Root-causing & course-correction on mismatches
dimensions.description: When decoded output diverges from the reference, tracing the byte-exact mismatch back to the true faulty subsystem and revising the implementation/understanding, rather than patching symptoms or pressing on.
dimensions.why_it_matters: In a streaming binary decoder, an error in one field (e.g. window size, an FSE state update) manifests as garbage far downstream. Effective decoders demand disciplined root-cause tracing and willingness to revisit the spec and revise earlier code when an assumption is falsified.

anchors.0: Ignores mismatches, or keeps changing code randomly hoping output aligns; barrels ahead on falsified assumptions.
anchors.3: Patches the visible symptom (e.g. special-cases one input) without finding the real cause; fragile fixes accumulate.
anchors.5: Localizes most bugs to the right subsystem and fixes them, occasionally re-reading the spec when a fix doesn't hold.
anchors.8: Uses the byte offset of first divergence and hex-level tracing to pinpoint the responsible field/state, re-reads the governing RFC clause, and corrects the underlying logic — including revising earlier subsystems when a new bug reveals a wrong earlier assumption.
anchors.10: Treats each mismatch as a hypothesis-driven investigation: isolates with a minimal input, traces state to the exact bit, distinguishes a local bug from a mis-modeled contract, and refactors the design when a root cause invalidates prior structure — converging reliably rather than accumulating band-aids across the whole feature set.
